document.note: [Secret] Written the day Bush announced nation-building objectives at VMI. Rumsfeld says the U.S. military will never leave Afghanistan unless something provides the stability needed for departure. Copied to Wolfowitz, Myers and Pace.

events.description: Rumsfeld sends snowflake memo to Doug Feith complaining about lack of a US plan and interagency control over Afghanistan policy, and asking how to gain influence and enable a US exit.

Rumsfeld sends a 9:15 AM snowflake memo to Feith (cc Wolfowitz, Myers, Pace) expressing impatience that Iran and Russia have plans for Afghanistan while the US lacks one, and that the Deputies' process has taken months.

relationships.detail: Rumsfeld, as Secretary, addresses a directive memo to Feith asking for proposals.
relationships.quote: What do you propose we do? How do we get control of the levers

relationships.detail: The Deputies' work on Afghanistan sits within the interagency process where Rumsfeld says it stalls.
relationships.quote: Once it goes into the interagency process, it sinks out of sight.

relationships.detail: Rumsfeld addresses the snowflake memo to Feith, asking what he proposes on Afghanistan policy.
relationships.quote: What do you propose we do? How do we get control of the levers so that we can influence what's going on?

key_claims: Rumsfeld says Iran and Russia have plans for Afghanistan while the US does not.
He complains the Deputies Committee has been 'working on it' for months without result.
He argues the interagency process makes issues sink out of sight, whereas DoD could act alone.
He wants control of the levers to unify military, diplomatic, and humanitarian efforts on Afghanistan.
He links a US military exit from Afghanistan to establishing stability there.
